p: as they spake unto the people: There are none more commonly diligent or bold enemies of the Church than those who profess themselves to be the chief builders of it, but the more they rage, the more steadfastly the faithful servants of God continue.

captain of the temple: The Jews had certain troops for the guard and safety of the temple and holy things (see Mt 26:47). These garrisons had a captain, such as Eleazarus Ananias, the high Priest's son in the time of the war that was in Judea, being a very impudent and proud young man; Josephus, lib. 2, of the taking of Judea.
number of the men was about: While they thought to diminish the number, they actually increased it.
rulers: These were those who were members of the Sanhedrin, who were all from the tribe of Judah, until Herod came to power.
kindred of the high priest: From whom the high Priests were usually chosen and made. At this time the former high Priest was stepping down, and a new high Priest was being appointed.
And when they had set them: Against those who brag of a succession of persons, without a succession of doctrine, and by that means beat down the true ministers of the word, as much as they are able.
name: By what authority.
If we this day be examined: The wolves who come after true pastors plead their own cause and not God's, neither the cause of the Church.
Be it known unto you all: He is indeed a true shepherd that teaches his sheep to rest upon Christ alone as upon one that is not dead, but has conquered death, and has all rule in his own hands.

name: There is no other man, or no other power and authority at all; and this kind of speech was common among the Jews, and arose from this, that when we are in danger we call upon those at whose hands we look for help.
under heaven: Anywhere: and this shows us the largeness of Christ's kingdom.
given among men: Of God.

Now when they saw the boldness: The good liberty and boldness of the servants of God does yet this much good, that those who lay hidden under a mask of zeal at length betray themselves to indeed be wicked men.

ignorant men: The word used here is "idiot", which signifies a private man when it is used in reference to a magistrate: but with reference to sciences and studies, it signifies one that is unlearned, and with regard to honour and estimation, it implies one of base degree, and of no estimation.
conferred among themselves: Laid their heads together.
Saying: He that flatters himself in ignorance, at length comes to do open wickedness, and that against his own conscience.
But Peter and John answered and: We must obey men to whom we are subject, but especially and before all things we must obey God.
So when they had further threatened: The wicked are so far off from doing what they wish, that God uses them contrary to their desires to set forth his glory, which he gives them permission to do.
And being let go: The apostles share their troubles with the congregation.

And when they heard that: We should neither be afraid of the threats of our enemies, neither yet foolishly condemn their rage and madness against us: but we have to set against their force and malice an earnest thinking upon the power and good will of God (both which we manifestly behold in Christ) and so flee to the aid and assistance of our Father.

people of Israel: Although the people of Israel were but one people, yet the plural number is used here, not so much for the twelve tribes, every one of which counted as a people, but because of the great multitude of them, as though many nations had assembled themselves together, as in Jud 5:14.
do whatsoever: The wicked execute God's counsel, even though they think nothing of it, but they are not therefore without fault.
thy hand and thy counsel determined: You had determined by your absolute authority and power.
And when they had prayed: God witnesses to his Church by a visible sign that it is he that will establish it, by shaking the powers both of heaven and of earth.

And the multitude of them that: An example of the true Church, in which there is equal consent both in doctrine and in charity toward one another: and the pastors deliver true doctrine both sincerely and constantly.
one heart and of one soul: They agreed in counsel, will, and all plans.
Neither was there any among them: True charity helps the need of the poor with its own loss, but in such a way that all things are done well and orderly.
